text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Commodore Plus/4 was released in 1984 as part of Commodore's attempt to create a more affordable business-oriented home computer. It was based on the same technology family as the Commodore 16 but included 64 KB of memory and built-in productivity software known as the "3 Plus 1" package. The system included word processing, spreadsheet, database, and graphing applications stored in ROM. Unlike the Commodore 64, the Plus/4 used the TED chipset and was not compatible with C64 software or hardware accessories. Its game library was smaller, although several titles were developed specifically for the system. The Plus/4 was discontinued after a short production run but remains notable for its built-in applications and place in Commodore's 8-bit computer lineup.
